To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) Language models trained on large Twitter corpora can be used as a feature extractor for implicit emotion prediction, 2) The use of attention mechanisms can improve the results, and 3) The use of ensembles of models trained on different data sets can also improve performance.
(1) transfer learning from language models is effective in predicting emotions, and (2) the combination of a language model with a CNN attention mechanism outperforms a language model alone.

(1) language models can be used to extract emotion-related features; (2) the combination of language models and neural networks is a powerful tool for the IEST; and (3) the use of attention mechanisms can improve the performance of neural networks.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of language models for emotion classification, as well as the use of attention-based neural networks for implicit emotions prediction.
the development and evaluation of a system for predicting emotions expressed in tweets without explicit mentions of those emotions.
the use of language models for the purpose of predicting emotion.
